chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who performed tawaf around the House eight circuits. He said: 'Is it a voluntary prayer or an obligatory one?' He said: 'Obligatory.' He said: 'He adds six [circuits] to it. When he finishes, he prays two rak'ahs at the Maqam Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Then he goes to al-Safa and al-Marwah and performs tawaf between them. When he finishes, he prays two more rak'ahs. Thus, it becomes a voluntary tawaf and an obligatory tawaf.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct ritual procedure when performing an extra voluntary tawaf alongside the obligatory one?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ritual mechanics of combining voluntary (*nafl*) and obligatory (*fard*) tawaf, specifically addressing the scenario where one has already completed eight circuits. The Imam instructs that the pilgrim should complete the remaining four circuits to reach the standard count of twelve, then perform the two rak'ahs of prayer at the Maqam Ibrahim before proceeding to Sa'i, thereby validating the combined act. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the accumulation of rewards and the structural integrity of Hajj rituals when voluntary acts are integrated with obligatory ones.
